summary: @servicetitan/cp-api preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. On `npm install`, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and immediately invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], {stdio:'inherit'})`. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line bundle heavily obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style rotating string-constant array (`function WV8StW(...){...MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())}`), a character-map alphabet-remap decoder (`hc1jfK9`), and hex-mangled identifiers. Using a freshly fetched alternate runtime to execute a large obfuscated payload at install time is an alternate-runtime dropper pattern that runs arbitrary code on the developer's machine while bypassing Node-focused static analysis. The package's declared surface is a near-empty API client (empty description, 136-byte main stub, small TypeScript stubs in dist/), which does not require a second language runtime or a 727KB obfuscated blob to function — the install-time payload is disproportionate to and disjoint from the advertised functionality. The `@servicetitan` scope framing raises additional scope-impersonation / account-compromise concerns.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
